items.title: [Editorial] Climate change and health: 10 years on, what next?
items.summary: The Paris Agreement came into force in 2016, a watershed in collective international action on climate change. That year also saw the creation of the Lancet Countdown on health and climate change, established to track the health effects of climate change and climate action. The past 10 years may have brought disheartening setbacks in climate policy, but there have also been huge advances in the understanding of and attitudes towards climate change.

items.title: [Comment] Offline: China bids to lead in global health
items.summary: China's last-minute nomination of Dr Song Li as a candidate for Director-General (DG) of WHO surprised many observers of global health politics. But from the perspective of an emerging superpower, it was not surprising at all. The Chinese Government is ready to assert its claim to positions of global leadership, especially now that the USA has turned its back on multilateralism. In Beijing last week, I sat down with Dr Li to listen to her set out her manifesto. She has four pillars supporting her pitch: a more efficient WHO; a safer world; equitable health systems; and harnessing innovation.

items.title: [Correspondence] Women with obstetric fistula in Somalia deserve better

items.title: Cardiac output monitoring using an automatic arm cuff device in surgical patients
items.summary: Pulse contour devices estimate cardiac output (CO) from an invasive arterial blood pressure waveform. However, arterial catheters are generally used only in higher-risk patients. By contrast, automatic arm cuff devices are used for noninvasive BP monitoring in almost all hospital patients. Furthermore, these devices measure cuff pressure oscillations, which are directly related to pulsatile blood volume rather than BP. We hypothesised that automatic arm cuff devices can offer an effective means to monitor CO.
